<p dir="auto"><strong>Windows Agent Arena (WAA) 🪟</strong> is a scalable Windows AI agent platform for testing and benchmarking multi-modal, desktop AI agents. WAA provides researchers and developers with a reproducible and realistic Windows OS environment for AI research, where agentic AI workflows can be tested across a diverse range of tasks.</p>
<p dir="auto">WAA supports the deployment of agents <strong>at scale</strong> using the Azure ML cloud infrastructure, allowing for the parallel running of multiple agents and delivering quick benchmark results for hundreds of tasks in minutes, not days.</p>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>2024-11-10: We added a new difficulty mode for Windows Agent Arena! You can try the new harder difficulty mode by changing the default <code>diff_lvl="normal"</code> to <code>diff_lvl="hard"</code> in <code>src/win-arena-container/start_client.sh</code>. Under the harder difficulty, in many tasks, agents must also learn to initialize/set up the task themselves (e.g., finding and opening the right program/application for the task) rather than have the task "set up" for them by the task config.</li>
<li>2024-10-30: We released the code for our Navi agent with Omniparser! For the top performing mode in the paper, run <code>./run-local.sh --som-origin mixed-omni --gpu-enabled true</code></li>
<li>2024-10-23: Microsoft open-sourced <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/OmniParser">Omniparser</a>, the current top performing screen understanding model in our benchmark.</li>
<li>2024-09-13: We released our <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.08264" rel="nofollow">paper</a>, <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsAgentArena">code</a>, <a href="https://microsoft.github.io/WindowsAgentArena" rel="nofollow">project page</a>, and <a href="https://www.microsoft.com/applied-sciences/projects/windows-agent-arena" rel="nofollow">blog post</a>. Check it out!</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">Before running the arena, you need to prepare a new WAA snapshot (also referred as WAA golden image). This 30GB snapshot represents a fully functional Windows 11 VM with all the programs needed to run the benchmark. This VM additionally hosts a Python server which receives and executes agent commands. To learn more about the components at play, see our <a href="/microsoft/WindowsAgentArena/blob/main/img/architecture-local.png">local</a> and <a href="/microsoft/WindowsAgentArena/blob/main/img/architecture-azure.png">cloud</a> components diagrams.</p>
<p dir="auto">To prepare the gold snapshot, run <strong>once</strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cd ./scripts
./run-local.sh --prepare-image true"><pre><span class="pl-c1">cd</span> ./scripts
./run-local.sh --prepare-image <span class="pl-c1">true</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">You can monitor progress at <code>http://localhost:8006</code>. The preparation process is fully automated and will take ~20 minutes.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Please do not interfere with the VM while it is being prepared. It will automatically shut down when the provisioning process is complete.</strong></p>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>During development, if you want to include any changes made in the <code>src/win-arena-container</code> directory in the WAA golden image, please ensure to specify the flag <code>--skip-build false</code> to the <code>run-local.sh</code> script (default to true). This will ensure that a new container image is built instead than using the prebuilt <code>windowsarena/winarena:latest</code> image.</li>
<li>If you have previously run an installation process and want to do it again from scratch, make sure to delete the content of <code>storage</code>.</li>
<li>We recommend copying this <code>storage</code> folder to a safe location outside of the repository in case you or the agent accidentally corrupt the VM at some point and you want to avoid a fresh setup.</li>
<li>Depending on your docker settings, you might have to run the above command with <code>sudo</code>.</li>
<li>Running on WSL2? If you encounter the error <code>/bin/bash: bad interpreter: No such file or directory</code>, we recommend converting the bash scripts from DOS/Windows format to Unix format:</li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">🌐 Azure Deployment -> Parallelizing the benchmark</h2><a id="user-content--azure-deployment---parallelizing-the-benchmark" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: 🌐 Azure Deployment -> Parallelizing the benchmark" href="#-azure-deployment---parallelizing-the-benchmark"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">1. <ul dir="auto">
<li>If you don't already have an Azure subscription, you can start a <a href="https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/" rel="nofollow">free trial</a>. Take note of the subscription id, we will use it as <code>AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID</code> in Section 3.</li>
<li>In the <a href="https://portal.azure.com/" rel="nofollow">Azure portal</a>, create a new resource group (e.g. <code>agents</code>) in the region of your choice. Take note of the resource group name, we will use it as <code>AZURE_ML_RESOURCE_GROUP</code> in Section 3.</li>
<li>Within this resource group, create an Azure Machine Learning resource (e.g. name it <code>agents_ml</code>). Take note of the ML workspace name, we will use it as <code>AZURE_ML_WORKSPACE_NAME</code> in Section 3. During the creation wizard, make sure to check the boxes for automatically creating new:
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Storage Account. <strong>Note:</strong> Take note of the Storage Account name, we will use it to upload the golden image in Section 2.</li>
<li>Key vault.</li>
<li>Application Insights.</li>
<li>[optional] Container Registry. You can use the Azure Container Registry to privately store your custom docker images without the need to push them to the public Docker Hub.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>

Copy the content of <code>scripts/azure_files/compute-instance-startup.sh</code> into this file and save it. Take note of the path where you save the file (in the form of <code>Users/<YOUR_USER>/compute-instance-startup.sh</code>), we will use it to run the script in Section 3.</li>
